query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** (October 2026) — Closest match: a meta-agent diagnoses training failures and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and RL configuration, applying validated changes during ongoing multi-turn RL.
   **People and affiliations:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

Its focus is workflow optimization rather than modifying a live training environment.
   **People and affiliations:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill).

Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** MIT, Stanford University and MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.21046v4)** — Closest broad research match: distinguishes **intra-test-time** adaptation within a task from **inter-test-time** learning across tasks, covering contextual learning, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. **People:** Huan-ang Gao, Jiayi Geng, Wenyue Hua, Mengkang Hu, and colleagues. **Affiliations:** Multi-institution collaboration including Princeton, Tsinghua, Carnegie Mellon, Penn State, and UIUC.

2. **[PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.26530v1)** — Combines live correction during an active run with persistent skills and memory for later runs; adapts the agent harness while keeping model backbones frozen. **People:** Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Wen Da, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan, Yao Hu, Wenjie Li, and Chengyue Jiang. **Affiliation:** AllSpark Team.

3. **[The What & When of Self-Evolving Agents](https://xinmingtu.cn/blog/2026/self-evolving-agents/)** — A concise conceptual framework separating updates to files, agent harnesses, and model weights, and whether improvements persist within or across sessions. **People and affiliations:** Xinming Tu — University of Washington and Phylo; Tong Chen — University of Washington.

4. **[Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.13417v1)** — Evaluates within-run behavior and experience reuse within and across tasks; relevant to measuring whether adaptation actually helps. **People and affiliations:** Yiwei Li and colleagues — Meituan; Wanli Yang, Hexiang Tan, and Fei Sun — University of Chinese Academy of Sciences.

1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — October 2026. A meta-agent adapts user simulators, environments, and training settings alongside the learning agent. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.24426v1)** — May 2026. Uses diagnosed tool-use failures to improve both the agent policy and its environment’s feedback. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Affiliations represented:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

3. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19682v1)** — December 2025. Co-trains an agent and a simulator that generates tasks matched to the agent’s evolving abilities. **People:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton and ByteDance Seed); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago).

4. **[Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.10299v1)** — August 2026. A survey covering agent–agent, agent–environment, and evolution-mechanism adaptation. **People:** Qing Zong, Jiayu Liu, Junhao Shen, Zecong Tang, Linsi Wu, Yuxuan Liu, Rui Wang, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Cheng Qian, Xiusi Chen, and Yangqiu Song. **Affiliations represented:** HKUST, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Chinese University of Hong Kong, University of Hong Kong, and Peking University.

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — The closest match: eight interactive tasks with online simulators and offline training datasets, including LLM-simulated human speakers. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, and Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (both).

2. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.22034v1)** — Simulated users gradually reveal preferences, testing whether agents clarify ambiguous goals and use tools effectively. Provides an environment for evaluation and training. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research and UIUC), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Zhiwei Liu, Jianguo Zhang, Haolin Chen, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://victorbarres.github.io/assets/html/tau2-bench-icml2026-oral.html)** — Tests multi-turn coordination where both the agent and simulated user can act through tools, particularly in technical support. **People:** Victor Barres and Soham Ray (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto, Vector Institute); Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra and Princeton Language & Intelligence).

4. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — A training framework integrating simulated users into RL, evaluated on τ-bench, τ²-bench, BFCL, and ACEBench. **People:** Weikang Zhao (Meituan and Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xili Wang (Meituan and Peking University); Chengdi Ma (Peking University); Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, and Xunliang Cai (Meituan).

text:

Nguyen (University College Cork); Quan Le (CeADAR, University College Dublin); Hoang Thanh Lam (IBM Research Dublin).

Qiu, and Yuqing Yang — Microsoft Research.
